opcache_enabled.ask: turn on OPcache for this site

generic.where: php.ini or a file in the PHP conf.d folder
steps: Install or enable the opcache extension (zend_extension=opcache).
Set opcache.enable=1 and restart PHP.
Tick opcache under Extensions.
If the extension list is not there, ask the host to enable OPcache.

opcache_coverage.ask: make OPcache cache the files under wp-content too, for example by removing wp-content from the OPcache blacklist (opcache.blacklist_filename) or the policy that excludes it

generic.where: The blacklist file named in php.ini, or the host's OPcache policy
steps: Open the file opcache.blacklist_filename points to and remove the line that matches wp-content.
Check that opcache.file_cache_only is 0.
Restart PHP so OPcache rereads the blacklist.
Remove the wp-content line from the blacklist file and reload Apache (apachectl graceful).

nginx.where: The PHP-FPM php.ini or conf.d folder
steps: Remove the wp-content line from the blacklist file and reload PHP-FPM (systemctl reload php8.x-fpm).

cloudways.where: Cloudways support, or the server's PHP settings over SSH
steps: Ask support to check the setting below. Paste the support ticket.

cpanel.where: cPanel > MultiPHP INI Editor, or the host
steps: Look for opcache.blacklist_filename in the editor and remove the wp-content entry from that file, or ask the host to do it.

opcache_memory.ask: raise opcache.memory_consumption for this site (to 256 MB, or what the server allows)

generic.where: php.ini or the PHP conf.d folder
steps: Raise opcache.memory_consumption (in MB), for example to 256.
Restart PHP.
Raise opcache.memory_consumption, or ask the host.

plesk.where: Plesk > Websites & Domains > PHP Settings > Additional directives
steps: Add opcache.memory_consumption=256.

opcache_strings.ask: raise opcache.interned_strings_buffer for this site, for example to 32 MB

generic.where: php.ini or the PHP conf.d folder
steps: Raise opcache.interned_strings_buffer (in MB), for example to 16 or 32.
Restart PHP.

opcache_keys.ask: raise opcache.max_accelerated_files for this site to at least {data.suggested}

generic.where: php.ini or the PHP conf.d folder
steps: Set opcache.max_accelerated_files above the number of PHP files (the measured value says how many).
Restart PHP.

opcache_restarts.ask: give OPcache more memory and file slots (opcache.memory_consumption, opcache.interned_strings_buffer and opcache.max_accelerated_files), as it keeps running out of room

generic.where: php.ini or the PHP conf.d folder
steps: Raise opcache.memory_consumption and opcache.max_accelerated_files until the restart counters stay at 0.
Restart PHP.

opcache_hit_rate.ask: look at why OPcache misses often: memory, file slots and opcache.revalidate_freq

generic.where: php.ini or the PHP conf.d folder
steps: Fix the other OPcache rows first: memory, strings and file slots.
Set opcache.revalidate_freq to 2 or more on production.

opcache_revalidate.ask: confirm that OPcache is flushed on every deploy and plugin update, as opcache.validate_timestamps is off

steps: Either set opcache.validate_timestamps=1 with opcache.revalidate_freq=2,
or keep it off and reload PHP-FPM (or call opcache_reset() in a web request) after every deploy and update.

object_cache_dropin.ask: set the Redis maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru (or volatile-lru) for this site's cache

generic.where: redis.conf, or the Redis service settings
steps: Set maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru so Redis drops old keys when full instead of refusing writes.

object_cache_roundtrip.ask: check the object cache backend (Redis or Memcached) for this site: the drop-in is installed but values do not survive from one request to the next

steps: Check that the cache service runs and the drop-in can connect (host, port, password in wp-config.php).
Look at the drop-in's own status screen or WP-CLI command for errors.
If you no longer use it, delete wp-content/object-cache.php.
Check the Redis add-on is active, or ask support.
Start Redis if it is stopped, then check the drop-in's settings.
Turn Memcached on again, or remove the drop-in.

wpengine.where: WP Engine User Portal > environment > Cache
steps: Check the object cache setting, or ask support. Paste the support ticket.
Ask support to check the setting below. Paste the support ticket.

object_cache_hit_rate.ask: check whether the object cache is too small or flushed often (maxmemory, evictions)

steps: Give the cache more memory if it evicts keys.
Look for plugins that flush the whole cache often.

php_branch.ask: move this site to PHP {data.newest} (or another branch that still gets security fixes)

generic.where: The host's control panel or the server's PHP packages
steps: Test the site on a newer PHP branch on staging first, then switch production.

wpengine.where: WP Engine User Portal > environment > PHP version
steps: Pick a newer version, after testing on staging.
Pick a newer version, after testing on staging.

cpanel.where: cPanel > MultiPHP Manager, or Select PHP Version
steps: Pick a newer version, after testing on staging.
Pick a newer version, after testing on staging.

php_patch.ask: update PHP to {data.latest}, the latest patch release of this branch

steps: Update the PHP packages (apt, yum or the host's panel) and restart PHP.

php_memory.ask: raise memory_limit for this site to at least 256M

steps: Raise memory_limit in php.ini (or .user.ini).
Set WP_MEMORY_LIMIT and WP_MAX_MEMORY_LIMIT in wp-config.php to what you need. WordPress can only raise it up to what PHP allows.
Raise memory_limit.

siteground.where: Site Tools > Devs > PHP Manager > PHP Variables
steps: Raise memory_limit.

hostinger.where: hPanel > Advanced > PHP Configuration > PHP options
steps: Raise memory_limit.
Raise memory_limit.

php_execution_time.ask: raise max_execution_time for this site to at least 60 seconds

steps: Raise max_execution_time. On nginx, also check fastcgi_read_timeout.
Raise max_execution_time.

php_input_vars.ask: raise max_input_vars for this site to {data.suggested}, as the menu "{data.menu}" has {data.items} items

steps: Raise max_input_vars above the number in Expected.
Restart PHP, or wait for .user.ini to be reread (5 minutes by default).
Raise max_input_vars.

siteground.where: Site Tools > Devs > PHP Manager > PHP Variables
steps: Raise max_input_vars.

hostinger.where: hPanel > Advanced > PHP Configuration > PHP options
steps: Raise max_input_vars.
Raise max_input_vars.

php_uploads.ask: set post_max_size at least as high as upload_max_filesize

steps: Set post_max_size a little higher than upload_max_filesize.

php_display_errors.ask: turn off display_errors on this production site and log errors instead

steps: Set display_errors=Off and log_errors=On in php.ini.
Or in wp-config.php: define( 'WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY', false ); and @ini_set( 'display_errors', '0' );

php_realpath.ask: raise realpath_cache_size for this site, for example to 4096K

steps: Raise realpath_cache_size (and realpath_cache_ttl to 600).
Restart PHP.

db_autoload.ask: help turn autoload off for the large options listed

steps: Use Turn autoload off on the options you do not need on every page.
Or: wp axle-runtime-doctor autoload off <option>
Delete options from plugins you removed (Axle Leftovers can do it with an undo).

db_slow_queries.ask: look at the slow queries listed, as they run on key pages

steps: Find the component that sends each slow query.
Update or replace that plugin, or add the index it needs. A persistent object cache hides many of them.

db_myisam.ask: convert the MyISAM tables listed to InnoDB

steps: Back up first.
Then for each table: wp db query "ALTER TABLE <table> ENGINE=InnoDB"

db_primary_keys.ask: add primary keys to the tables listed

steps: Check which plugin owns each table and update it; most plugins add a key in a later version.
Back up before changing tables by hand.

db_version.ask: upgrade the database server to a supported MySQL or MariaDB release

generic.where: The host's control panel or the server packages
steps: Upgrade to a supported release after a backup and a test on staging.

cron_mode.ask: add a real cron job for this site that runs WP-Cron every 5 minutes, as DISABLE_WP_CRON is set and nothing runs due events

steps: Add: */5 * * * * wget -q -O - {site}/wp-cron.php?doing_wp_cron > /dev/null 2>&1
Or with WP-CLI: */5 * * * * cd /path/to/site && wp cron event run --due-now > /dev/null 2>&1
Or remove DISABLE_WP_CRON from wp-config.php.
Add a job every 5 minutes that calls wp-cron.php (command in the generic fix).
Add a task every 5 minutes that fetches {site}/wp-cron.php.
Add a job every 5 minutes that calls wp-cron.php.
Add a job every 5 minutes that calls wp-cron.php.
Add a job every 5 minutes that calls wp-cron.php.

wpengine.where: WP Engine User Portal > environment > Utilities, or support
steps: Ask support to turn on their alternate cron for this environment. Paste the support ticket.
Ask support to set up a server cron for wp-cron.php. Paste the support ticket.
List them: wp cron event list --fields=hook,next_run_relative,args
Delete extras: wp cron event delete <hook>, then let the plugin schedule it once again.
Update the plugin that schedules them, as it schedules without checking first.

loopback.ask: let the server reach the site directly (for example through a hosts entry pointing the site's domain to 127.0.0.1), or allow the server's own IP past the firewall

generic.where: The CDN or firewall rules, or /etc/hosts on the server
steps: Allow the server's own IP in the firewall or CDN bot rules.
Or point the site's domain to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts on the server, so loopback requests stay local.
chmod 640 wp-config.php (or 600 when PHP runs as the file owner).

fs_uploads_php.ask: help investigate the PHP files found in the uploads folder

steps: Take a backup for evidence, then look at each file. If you did not put it there, treat the site as hacked: change passwords and salts, update everything, remove the files.
Block PHP in uploads in the web server config.

fs_ownership.ask: make PHP run as the user that owns the WordPress files (or change the owner to that user)

steps: chown -R <php-user>:<group> on the WordPress folder, or run PHP-FPM as the file owner.
Remove FS_METHOD from wp-config.php once they match.

fs_content_writable.ask: make wp-content writable for PHP, or confirm that it is read-only on purpose

steps: Make wp-content writable for the PHP user (755 for folders, owned by that user).

fs_disk.ask: add disk space to this site or help find what fills it

generic.where: The host's control panel or the server
steps: Look for old backups, logs and caches under wp-content first.
Add space if the site really needs it.
